defects: O3: ἐν κρυπτῷ (The page has a different Greek phrase that looks like ἐν σκοτεινῷ ("in darkness"). The candidate put in the wording of the Greek New Testament at John 18:20 instead.)
O10: ἀπροκαλύπτως (The page prints ἀκροαματικὰ ("esoteric teachings", the opposite of ἐξωτερικὰ). The candidate's word means "openly", so the contrast the author is drawing is lost.)
containment_candidates.note: The Latin is accurate throughout, but two of the three small Greek glosses are wrong: one has been replaced with the Gospel's own wording and the other with a word that means something different.

defects: O1: The left shield displays the Chigi family arms (six mountain (The arms are show-through from the other side of the leaf, not printed on this page. The Chigi and Pamphili identifications are invented: the left shield is crowned with fleurs-de-lis (French royal arms).)
O1: representing Pope Innocent X, surmounted by the papal tiara (The right shield is identified as Pamphili / Innocent X with no basis in the image. The faint text behind it names Clement VIII.)
containment_candidates.note: The two imprimaturs are right, but abbreviations are silently expanded, and the coats of arms (really show-through) are wrongly said to be Alexander VII and Innocent X when the reverse text names Clement VIII.

defects: I1: Tanta hujus, quod suam proxime metam constitutum videmus, se (The image is a blank white leaf with no text, initial or catchword. The whole transcription belongs to another leaf, or is not on this page at all.)
O14: A large decorative woodcut initial 'T' that begins the first (Describes a decorated initial with a grapevine and a sun face, but no image appears on this blank leaf.)
containment_candidates.note: The scan shows a completely blank page, but a full page of Latin preface text is printed beside it, so the transcription does not match this image.

defects: I1: [...scriptam], operae fore pretium, existimamus: Deum castig (The candidate is the closing page of the same Gera program (Peace of Ryswick, the two student orators, the 'Proposuit publice Gerae' colophon and notes a–e). The image is the opening page, which begins with the woodcut initial and 'Tanta hujus, quod suam proxime metam constitutum videmus, seculi rerum…', covers church history, Jaeger of Tübingen and the century's inventions, and ends with the catchword 'nem'. None of the page's text appears.)
containment_candidates.note: The transcription doesn't match the image. The page shows the program's opening ('Tanta hujus… seculi'), with church history and inventions like the camera obscura and microscopes, but the text beside it is the closing page about the Peace of Ryswick and the two student orators.

defects: I1: Iugera producunt spatiis precincta duobus ... Axenotridas su (Entire text is from another page of the same poem (Greece and the Peloponnese). The leaf reads 'Quinq; uomunt amnem quam se procul insula teuce ... Oceani uicina salo qua glauca recumbit' (Scythia, Danube, Thrace).)

defects: I1: Matutina ferens solitos per sydere cursus … Flatus at gemini (The candidate is 38 lines of weather-sign verse that this page does not contain. The page has a woodcut of Hydra, the Crater and the raven, then 13 lines of prose beginning 'Ydra sup cui caudā coruū sedere dicūt'. defects: I1: Nam quæ per bis sex signorum labier orbe (The whole candidate is a different passage of the poem: planets, the Milky Way and Perseus. Probably another leaf's text, but it could also be invented.)

O5: Hunc orionis sub læua cernere planta (None of the page's real lines are transcribed. They run from 'Hic ubi se pariter' to 'Hunc orionis sub læua cernere planta', and the quoted line is the page's last, which the candidate doesn't contain.)
